title: Shoulder wrap in cluster stitch
subtitle: A square of treble clusters separated by ch-1 spaces in DK weight, worn folded as a triangle
excerpt: This square wrap is worked in rows of three-treble clusters separated by ch-1 spaces on a 4 mm hook with DK yarn. The 90 x 90 cm square folds diagonally and is worn as a shoulder triangle. The cluster stitch creates an open, textured fabric that is lighter than solid treble but more structured than a mesh.

glossaryTerms.definition: Work 3 trebles into the same ch-1 space, leaving the last loop of each on the hook (4 loops on hook), then yarn over and pull through all 4 loops. The three trebles join at the top to form one compact stitch.

content.text: This shoulder wrap is a 90 cm square worked in rows of three-treble clusters separated by ch-1 spaces. Fold it diagonally before wearing and drape the long straight edge across the back of the neck; the two corners of the fold hang in front. At DK weight on a 4 mm hook the fabric is open enough to show the cluster texture but warm enough for cooler weather. The whole piece is one rectangle with no shaping.
A
treble cluster (cl)

is three trebles worked into the same ch-1 space, all joined at the top. Each cluster sits in a ch-1 space from the previous row; on each new row you work into the spaces from the row below, not into the cluster tops. The pattern repeat is: 1 cl in next ch-1 space, ch 1; worked across the row.

attrs.title: Materials
attrs.body: Approximately 350 g DK-weight yarn. A 4 mm crochet hook (US G/6). Tapestry needle. Craft scissors. Blocking mat and pins. Tape measure.

content.text: Gauge

5 cluster repeats (cl + ch 1) x 8 rows = 10 x 10 cm in DK yarn with a 4 mm hook, measured unstretched. Work a swatch of at least 20 clusters wide and 16 rows deep, measure the central 10 cm, and adjust hook size before beginning.
Stitches used
chain (ch): UK and US shared.
slip stitch (sl st): UK and US shared.
treble (tr): UK; the same move as US "double crochet" (dc).
treble cluster (cl): 3 trebles into the same space, joined at the top as described above.
Pattern
The square is worked flat. The foundation chain is one side of the square; the rows build the other side. The stitch count in clusters stays constant throughout at 45 clusters per row.
Foundation chain
Ch 137. (This gives 45 cluster positions plus selvedge chains.)
Row 1 (right side)
Ch 4 (counts as 1 tr + ch 1). Skip 3 ch. *1 cl in next ch-3 group (insert into the centre chain), ch 1, skip 2 ch*; repeat from * to * to last 3 ch. 1 tr in last ch. Turn. (45 cl, 46 ch-1 spaces)
Row 2
Ch 4 (counts as 1 tr + ch 1). *1 cl in next ch-1 space, ch 1*; repeat from * to * to end. 1 tr in the top of the ch-4 turning chain. Turn. (45 cl, 46 ch-1 spaces)
Continue to approximately row 72
Repeat row 2 until the piece measures 90 cm from the foundation chain edge, approximately 72 rows. The stitch count remains 45 cl throughout. Fasten off.
Finishing

Fasten off and weave in both ends securely. A single row of double crochet worked around all four edges gives clean, stable selvedges. Wet-block by soaking, pressing out water, then pinning to 90 x 90 cm. Check that all four corners are true right angles before leaving to dry.
Care
Handwash in cool water with mild soap. Lay flat to dry. Do not tumble-dry.
What to try next

Increase the cluster to five trebles for a larger, more open texture. Work the square in two colours by alternating stripes of two rows each; the ch-1 spaces pick up both colours cleanly. A pointed fringe along two sides of the square transforms it from a shoulder wrap into a triangular shawl.
